summary: Validated Kitchen BEO v2 (days→tandas + change-detection + batch print) end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest pass on /api/kitchen-beo/event/{id} (shape: event_id, event_name, calendar_dates, guest_count, days[{date, tandas, tanda_count}], totals{days_count,tandas_count,recipes_count}, snapshot_hash, last_print, changed_since_print, allergens_aggregate, dietary_tags_aggregate), no price/cost/unit_price fields anywhere, 1 day 2026-05-20 with exactly 3 tandas (Desayuno/Almuerzo/Coffee), each with extras list. mark-printed POST returns {success, log_id, printed_at}; re-GET shows changed_since_print=false; mark-printed with a different snapshot then re-GET shows changed_since_print=true with last_print still populated. /api/kitchen-beo/batch?start_date=&end_date= returns sheets_count + sheets[] sorted by first date, defaults to Won/Committed/Confirmed, includes event_test_timed_services. Regression test_sprint4_culinary_phase2.py::test_kitchen_beo_endpoint still passes. Frontend (Pame Mey, food-ops module enabled): /food-ops/kitchen-sheets (Kitchen Sheets tab inside Culinary Intelligence) renders KitchenSheetsBatch with all testids (batch-start-date, batch-end-date, batch-refresh, batch-toggle-all, batch-print-btn, batch-row-{id}); selecting a row and clicking Print injects an iframe, calls window.print() exactly 1x, POSTs /mark-printed (1 XHR detected), toast 'X sheet(s) printed and marked' appears, and the row badge flips to green 'printed' with 'Last print: …· Pame Mey' line.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py L4492-4500 (list_kitchen_beo_batch): reuses `await get_kitchen_beo(ev['event_id'], user)` inside a per-event loop — that's N+1 round-trips to MongoDB for events, order_items and recipes. For an org with hundreds of confirmed events in the range this will be slow. Consider batching the order_items and recipe lookups across all selected events.

server.py L4421: `snapshot_hash = (payload or {}).get('snapshot_hash') or ''` — empty string is stored when caller omits it, which then sets changed_since_print=True forever on next read because '' != real_hash. Either reject missing snapshot_hash with 400 or copy the current real snapshot server-side when missing.

server.py L4360-4375 build snapshot_hash from `repr()` of a Python tuple — repr ordering depends on dict iteration but here it's a list so it's stable; still, floats like 12.0 vs 12 will produce different reprs ('12.0' vs '12') and thus phantom drift. Coerce numerics to a normalized form before hashing.

KitchenSheetsBatch.js L75-99: the print iframe is appended, written to and removed within 1.5s — on slow Windows printers the print dialog may not have appeared yet when the iframe is detached, which can cancel the print. Consider waiting on iframe.contentWindow.onafterprint before cleanup.

KitchenSheetsBatch.js L89-98: Promise.all(...).then() fires fetchSheets() but the toast and refresh aren't awaited from the click handler — if the user clicks Print rapidly twice, both runs race. Disable batch-print-btn while a print cycle is in flight.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the batch-print path actually exercised (page render, all testids present, select→print→iframe→window.print()→mark-printed POST→toast→badge transition all verified). Single-event dialog and DocumentPreview clone-print not interactively exercised this round — see action_items.
